rows.consequence: A transient SSH, SCP, timeout, or post-marker failure can delete the sole status and raw measurement evidence, preventing diagnosis and offline replay. If the remote worker is still running after transport loss, deletion also races its writes. This is evidence-loss behavior and therefore a blocker under the charter.
rows.counterevidence: Successful collection copies every flat artifact into memory before cleanup, cleanup outcomes are reported, and a failed rm may leave recoverable data. The protocol also requires cleanup after collection and status parsing. Those safeguards do not protect the failure branches, which invoke cleanup before those prerequisites hold.
evidence_refs: Bounded absence search across manifest tests for collect/post-marker failure retention found structured-failure assertions but no assertion that uncollected remote evidence survives.
rows.finding: NodeWorkerClient performs destructive remote cleanup before evidence custody is established. Worker-command transport failure, post-task clock-marker failure, and artifact-collection failure all immediately route through rm -rf of the remote task and artifact paths, even though status/raw artifacts were not safely collected or parsed.

rows.consequence: A stale, path-collided, or future-version status can be silently attributed to the wrong task and accepted as success. Schema evolution can therefore change artifact semantics without a rejection/migration path, while persisted bundle metadata lacks the formal status schema version needed to select an offline replay parser.
rows.counterevidence: The current worker writes status atomically with protocol_version 1, per-task directories reduce accidental collision, input task versions are rejected strictly, and the real subprocess parity test exercises the normal v1 producer/consumer pair. None of those checks validate the collected response at the client boundary.
evidence_refs: Bounded BASE_HEAD search found no NodeWorkerClient response-version or request-identity validation and no mismatch negative test; raw_status task_id consumers only name copied log files.
rows.finding: The client does not validate status.json protocol_version or correlate task_id, task_type, operation, or node_role with the dispatched request. It treats any collected object whose status string is 'succeeded' as success. The formal response protocol version is then not propagated by the runtime/telemetry metadata adapters; only the open worker metadata dictionary is retained.

rows.finding: FIRST SPLIT BREAK / weakest schema seam: the protocol advertises task_type as an open enum with future transfer-send/transfer-receive tasks, but worker validation closes the payload discriminator to runtime, workload, or telemetry and requires exactly one of those blocks. The future-task test passes only by attaching a telemetry block to transfer-send, so it does not represent a real transfer payload.

rows.consequence: Local and remote execution silently disagree about the same application failure. On future transfer/file operations, an on-node permission error can be misreported as connectivity loss and trigger W3-001's destructive early cleanup instead of collecting the worker's structured permission/status evidence.
rows.counterevidence: Real SSH authentication/name-resolution failures commonly use the matched phrases and normally exit 255, so the heuristic catches useful transport cases. Existing tests cover returncode 255 authentication and a generic returncode 3 application failure, but not a non-255 application error containing a heuristic phrase.
evidence_refs: Pinned in-memory behavior trace: RunnerCompleted(returncode=3, stderr='Permission denied opening /data on node') produced failure_reason=transport_unavailable and ssh_error_class=ssh_transport.
rows.finding: SSH failure classification treats selected stderr phrases as transport failure regardless of return code. Thus an on-node application failure such as returncode 3 with 'Permission denied' is classified transport_unavailable, whereas the local transport classifies an ordinary nonzero command as unknown_error. NodeWorkerClient then treats the SSH result as transport loss and skips authoritative status collection.
